label: Tide-Man the Blue first encounter

purpose.value: The ferryman and keeper of the floodgates holds the water still long enough to hail the armed stranger and issue the law's fair warning; the hero hears every word and misreads a rescue service as a drowning horror. The guardian attempts communication first; the hero misreads it as a villain's taunt.

emotionalProgression.note: The guardian announces itself and its duty plainly, framed by ferries and floodgates.
The warning was honest and complete; being ignored reads as insult.

notes: The scene MUST establish the guardian announcing itself and warning honestly — the law of fair warning means its attack paths will be shown, not hidden. The mercy exit (withdraw) is offered and never taken. Flavor: ferries and floodgates. The player's view may hint the guardian's true role; the hero must not perceive it.
